Disability evaluation is the determination of the degree of a physical, mental, or emotional handicap. The diagnosis is applied to legal qualification for benefits and income under disability insurance and to eligibility for Social Security and Workers' Compensation benefits. The evaluation depends on the type of coverage.

section.type: Disability evaluation for social security administration
section.heading: Disability evaluation for social security administration

list.listitem: Disability benefits are paid to 7.5 million people totaling $76 billion per year. Conditions making the greatest contribution to years lived with disability are low back pain, major depressive disorders, neck pain, and anxiety disorders.

Mental health conditions are the most common disorders, accounting for 36 percent of beneficiaries. A multifaceted intervention can increase the likelihood of paid employment and qualty of life in these patients. B
Musculoskeletal system and connective tissue disorders are the second most common disability, accounting for 23 percent; this includes joint and spine disorders, fractures, and amputation.
A study of twins in Finland found that heavy drinking in early adulthood increased the likelihood of disability later in life.

list.listitem: Provides benefits to individuals who are insured through Social Security premiums paid while persons are employed and to certain disabled dependents of individuals.
Federal benefits are managed by regional social security offices.

list.listitem: Supplemental security income provides benefits to help aged, blind, and disabled people who have little or no income.
Benefit is from general tax revenue and provides cash to meet basic needs for food, clothing, and shelter.

section.type: Social security administration definition of disability
section.heading: Social security administration definition of disability

list.listitem: “Inability to engage in any substantial gainful activity by reason of any medically determinable physical or mental impairment which can be expected to result in death or has lasted or can be expected to last for a continuous period of not less than 12 months, or blindness ....”

Medically determinable impairmenta: "An impairment that results from anatomical, physiological, or psychological abnormalities which can be shown by medically acceptable clinical and laboratory diagnostic techniques.”

Substantial gainful activity: “... considering age, education, and work experience, any ... kind of substantial gainful work which exists in the national economy, regardless of whether such work exists in the immediate area in which he lives, or whether a specific job vacancy exists for him, or whether he would be hired if he applied for work.”
State disability determination services, which are federally funded state agencies, are responsible for developing medical evidence and rendering initial determination of disability.
Evidence is obtained from claimant's medical records, and if insufficient a consultative exam from an independent source will be performed.
Determination is made by two-person adjudicative team, including a medical or psychological consultant and a disability examiner.
The treating physician does not determine disability but may be asked to provide objective evidence of the claimant's impairments and limitations.

The treating physician is an important source of medical evidence due to longitudinal documentation of claimant's impairments. The Social Security Administration may request medical reports from physicians or psychologists.

Reports include medical history, clinical findings, laboratory findings, diagnosis, treatment with response, and prognosis. Additionally a statement should provide an opinion about what the claimant can still do despite his or her impairment(s), based on the medical source's findings. The statement should include ability to sit, stand, walk, lift, carry, and handle objects, and extent of hearing, speaking, and traveling impairments. For mental impairments the statement should include ability to understand, carry out, and remember instructions and to respond appropriately to supervision, coworkers, and work pressures in a work setting. The opinion should be based on medical findings and objectively state why the impairments limit the claimant's work activity.

feature.caption: Tips for Physicians of Disability Claimants.

list.listitem: Disability evaluation can be time-consuming and frustrating, so be honest and tell patients what you are able to do.

A medical record, including an objective functional impact of work-related and non-work-related injuries and chronic disabling conditions will usually satisfy evidentiary requirements of disability agencies. Common activities such as house chores and grocery shopping can be used to evaluate unemployed individuals.

Physician statements should provide pertinent historical and physical documentation of the claimant's impairment and provide supporting facts of why the claimant's impairment is a disability. For example, state whether the claimant is unable to stoop or kneel because of reduced range of motion of lumbar spine, which is disabling in the patient's occupation as a plumber.
Disability evaluation under Social Security, or the “blue book,” provides criteria for disability for most impairments and can be accessed at: http://www.ssa.gov/disability/professionals/bluebook/.
